thesis_refs.cite: Beaman et al. 2012, Female Leadership Raises Aspirations and Educational Attainment for Girls: A Policy Experiment in India
thesis_refs.finding: Randomly assigned reservation of village council leadership for women in West Bengal closed part of the gender gap in aspirations and erased the gender gap in adolescent educational attainment.

thesis_refs.cite: Macchiavello et al. 2020, Challenges of Change: An Experiment Promoting Women to Managerial Roles in the Bangladeshi Garment Sector
thesis_refs.finding: Trained marginal female supervisor candidates, randomly assigned to lines, were initially less productive than male candidates, but the gaps disappeared after four to six months.

thesis_refs.cite: Bryan, Chowdhury & Mobarak 2014, Underinvestment in a Profitable Technology: The Case of Seasonal Migration in Bangladesh
thesis_refs.finding: An $8.50 incentive induced 22 percent of rural Bangladeshi households to send a lean-season migrant, raised origin consumption and raised re-migration one and three years later.

thesis_refs.cite: Hussam, Rigol & Roth 2022, Targeting High Ability Entrepreneurs Using Community Information
thesis_refs.finding: In a cash grant experiment in India, community rankings identified microentrepreneurs with higher returns to capital, but peers distorted rankings when they influenced allocation; simple incentive mechanisms realigned them.

thesis_refs.cite: Egger et al. 2022, General Equilibrium Effects of Cash Transfers: Experimental Evidence from Kenya
thesis_refs.finding: One-time unconditional cash transfers of about USD 1,000 to poor rural Kenyan households raised recipients' consumption and assets, with large spillovers to non-recipients and firms and minimal price inflation.

thesis_refs.cite: Bandiera et al. 2017, Labor Markets and Poverty in Village Economies
thesis_refs.finding: A nationwide Bangladeshi programme transferring livestock and skills to the poorest women moved them into livestock rearing and raised their earnings, assets and consumption for at least four years.

thesis_refs.cite: Balboni et al. 2022, Why Do People Stay Poor?
thesis_refs.finding: Around a randomised livestock transfer to ultra-poor Bangladeshi households, those pushed above an asset threshold accumulated assets and moved into better occupations, while those below slid back.

thesis_refs.cite: Chetty, Hendren & Katz 2016, The Effects of Exposure to Better Neighborhoods on Children: New Evidence from the Moving to Opportunity Experiment
thesis_refs.finding: Housing vouchers to move to lower-poverty neighbourhoods raised college attendance and earnings for children who moved before age 13, with slightly negative effects for adolescents.

thesis_refs.cite: Kling, Liebman & Katz 2007, Experimental Analysis of Neighborhood Effects
thesis_refs.finding: Moving to Opportunity housing vouchers moved families to safer, lower-poverty neighbourhoods but had no significant overall effect on adult economic self-sufficiency or physical health.

thesis_refs.cite: Duflo 2001, Schooling and Labor Market Consequences of School Construction in Indonesia
thesis_refs.finding: Each INPRES primary school built per 1,000 children raised education by 0.12 to 0.19 years and wages by 1.5 to 2.7 percent for exposed cohorts.

thesis_refs.cite: Duflo 2004, The Medium Run Effects of Educational Expansion: Evidence from a Large School Construction Program in Indonesia
thesis_refs.finding: The INPRES school construction programme raised education for young cohorts, and the resulting rise in primary graduates lowered older cohorts' wages and raised their formal participation.

thesis_refs.cite: Card, Domnisoru & Taylor 2022, The Intergenerational Transmission of Human Capital: Evidence from the Golden Age of Upward Mobility
thesis_refs.finding: Upward educational mobility in 1940 was strongly tied to teacher wages, including across Southern state borders where minimum teacher salary laws created sharp wage differences.

thesis_refs.cite: Hardy & McCasland 2023, Are Small Firms Labor Constrained? Experimental Evidence from Ghana
thesis_refs.finding: Randomly placing unemployed young people as apprentices with small Ghanaian firms raised firm size by about half a worker and profits by about 10 percent per placement offered.

thesis_refs.cite: Carranza et al. 2022, Job Search and Hiring with Limited Information about Workseekers' Skills
thesis_refs.finding: Giving South African workseekers skill assessment results they can credibly share with firms raised their employment and earnings and better aligned their beliefs and search.

thesis_refs.cite: Bassi & Nansamba 2022, Screening and Signalling Non-Cognitive Skills: Experimental Evidence from Uganda
thesis_refs.finding: Disclosing certificates on young Ugandan workers' non-cognitive skills during job interviews raised expectations and managers' assessments, increased assortative matching and raised earnings conditional on employment.

thesis_refs.cite: Abebe et al. 2021, Anonymity or Distance? Job Search and Labour Market Exclusion in a Growing African City
thesis_refs.finding: A job application workshop helping young jobseekers signal skills raised formal and stable employment and, four years later, earnings, while transport subsidy effects dissipated.

thesis_refs.cite: McCaig 2011, Exporting Out of Poverty: Provincial Poverty in Vietnam and U.S. Market Access
thesis_refs.finding: Vietnamese provinces more exposed to US tariff cuts under the 2001 Bilateral Trade Agreement saw faster poverty reduction and faster wage growth for the least educated.

thesis_refs.cite: McCaig & Pavcnik 2018, Export Markets and Labor Allocation in a Low-Income Country
thesis_refs.finding: US tariff cuts under the US-Vietnam Bilateral Trade Agreement raised the formal-sector share of Vietnamese manufacturing workers by 5 percentage points.

thesis_refs.cite: Topalova 2010, Factor Immobility and Regional Impacts of Trade Liberalization: Evidence on Poverty from India
thesis_refs.finding: Rural Indian districts more exposed to the 1991 tariff cuts saw slower poverty decline and consumption growth, most among the least mobile poor and in states with inflexible labour laws.

thesis_refs.cite: Atkin, Khandelwal & Osman 2017, Exporting and Firm Performance: Evidence from a Randomized Experiment
thesis_refs.finding: Randomly assigned export orders raised Egyptian rug producers' profits by 16 to 26 percent and improved quality and technical efficiency, evidence of learning-by-exporting.

thesis_refs.cite: Bau & Matray 2023, Misallocation and Capital Market Integration: Evidence from India
thesis_refs.finding: Staggered liberalisation of foreign capital access across Indian industries reduced capital misallocation and raised aggregate productivity, with the largest gains at initially high-MRPK firms.

thesis_refs.cite: Hsieh & Moretti 2019, Housing Constraints and Spatial Misallocation
thesis_refs.finding: Stringent housing supply restrictions in high-productivity US cities limited workers' access to them and lowered aggregate US growth by 36 percent from 1964 to 2009.

thesis_refs.cite: Bloom et al. 2013, Does Management Matter? Evidence from India
thesis_refs.finding: Free management consulting randomly given to Indian textile plants raised productivity by 17 percent in the first year and led to more plants within three years.

thesis_refs.cite: Bruhn, Karlan & Schoar 2018, The Impact of Consulting Services on Small and Medium Enterprises: Evidence from a Randomized Trial in Mexico
thesis_refs.finding: A year of subsidised management consulting for Mexican SMEs raised TFP and return on assets and increased employment and wage bill by about 50 percent five years later.

thesis_refs.cite: de Mel, McKenzie & Woodruff 2014, Business Training and Female Enterprise Start-up, Growth, and Dynamics: Experimental Evidence from Sri Lanka
thesis_refs.finding: The ILO SIYB business training changed business practices of Sri Lankan women in business but had no impact on profits, sales or capital stock.

thesis_refs.cite: Banerjee & Duflo 2014, Do Firms Want to Borrow More? Testing Credit Constraints Using a Directed Lending Program
thesis_refs.finding: Indian firms gaining and then losing priority-sector directed credit eligibility expanded and then contracted borrowing, sales and profits, showing severe credit constraints.

thesis_refs.cite: McKenzie 2017, Identifying and Spurring High-Growth Entrepreneurship: Experimental Evidence from a Business Plan Competition
thesis_refs.finding: Randomly awarded grants of about US$50,000 in Nigeria's YouWiN! competition raised firm entry, survival, profits, sales and employment over five years.

thesis_refs.cite: Blattman & Dercon 2018, The Impacts of Industrial and Entrepreneurial Work on Income and Health
thesis_refs.finding: In Ethiopia an entrepreneurship programme of $300 plus business training raised earnings 33 percent, while industrial job offers had no income effect and raised health problems.

thesis_refs.cite: Blattman, Fiala & Martinez 2014, Generating Skilled Self-Employment in Developing Countries: Experimental Evidence from Uganda
thesis_refs.finding: Unsupervised group grants of $382 per member to young adults in conflict-affected northern Uganda raised business assets 57 percent, hours 17 percent and earnings 38 percent after four years.

thesis_refs.cite: de Mel, McKenzie & Woodruff 2013, The Demand for, and Consequences of, Formalization among Informal Firms in Sri Lanka
thesis_refs.finding: Information and reimbursement of registration costs did not induce Sri Lankan informal firms to register, while payments of one-half to two months' profits induced one-fifth to one-half.

thesis_refs.cite: Banerjee et al. 2015, The Miracle of Microfinance? Evidence from a Randomized Evaluation
thesis_refs.finding: Randomly opening microcredit branches in Hyderabad slums raised borrowing and business investment but left average consumption and business profits unchanged.

thesis_refs.cite: Meager 2019, Understanding the Average Impact of Microcredit Expansions: A Bayesian Hierarchical Analysis of Seven Randomized Experiments
thesis_refs.finding: Pooling seven randomised microcredit evaluations, the impact on household business and consumption is unlikely to be transformative and may be negligible, with moderate cross-site heterogeneity.

thesis_refs.cite: Bari et al. 2024, Asset-Based Microfinance for Microenterprises: Evidence from Pakistan
thesis_refs.finding: Offering microcredit clients hire-purchase finance for an asset worth four times their usual limit produced large, persistent gains in business size, profits and household consumption.

thesis_refs.cite: Abebe et al. 2021, Anonymity or Distance? Job Search and Labour Market Exclusion in a Growing African City
thesis_refs.finding: A job application workshop helping young jobseekers signal skills raised formal and stable employment and, four years later, earnings, while transport subsidy effects dissipated.

thesis_refs.cite: Franklin 2018, Location, Search Costs and Youth Unemployment: Experimental Evidence from Transport Subsidies
thesis_refs.finding: Randomly assigned transport subsidies raised job search intensity and the likelihood that unemployed youth in urban Ethiopia found good, permanent jobs.

thesis_refs.cite: Guner, Ventura & Xu 2008, Macroeconomic Implications of Size-Dependent Policies
thesis_refs.finding: In a calibrated growth model, policies restricting large establishments or subsidising small ones enough to cut average size by 20 percent substantially reduce output.

thesis_refs.cite: Restuccia & Rogerson 2008, Policy Distortions and Aggregate Productivity with Heterogeneous Establishments
thesis_refs.finding: Policies that make individual producers face different prices reallocate resources to less productive establishments and can cut output and measured TFP by 30 to 50 percent.

thesis_refs.cite: Do & Iyer 2008, Land Titling and Rural Transition in Vietnam
thesis_refs.finding: Vietnam's 1993 Land Law raised the share of area under long-term crops and labour devoted to nonfarm work, driven mainly by greater tenure security rather than credit.

thesis_refs.cite: Blattman, Fiala & Martinez 2014, Generating Skilled Self-Employment in Developing Countries: Experimental Evidence from Uganda
thesis_refs.finding: Unsupervised group grants of $382 per member to young adults in conflict-affected northern Uganda raised business assets 57 percent, hours 17 percent and earnings 38 percent after four years.
